builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
summary: GEdit replaces unconstrained knowledge-editing methods (such as ROME/MEMIT-style weight updates and their sequential variants) with an LR+D factor model of FFN hidden representations that protects a low-rank core knowledge subspace and adapts regularization strength per edit difficulty. The cost is additional per-edit computation to estimate the representation geometry and calibrate editability, plus implementation complexity over existing editing libraries. It can fail if the assumed low-rank structure does not hold for a given model, if editability is miscalibrated (hard edits fail or easy edits corrupt pretrained knowledge), or if the method's benefits do not transfer beyond the evaluated GPT2-XL/GPT-J/LLaMA-3-8B settings.
rationale: Knowledge editing on consumer-scale models is feasible for this reader, but the abstract gives no quantified gains and no evidence on models or editing workloads the reader actually runs, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: Geometry-aware regularization for LLM knowledge editing

claims.statement: GEdit replaces unconstrained knowledge-editing methods (such as ROME/MEMIT-style weight updates and their sequential variants) with an LR+D factor model of FFN hidden representations that protects a low-rank core knowledge subspace and adapts regularization strength per edit difficulty. The cost is additional per-edit computation to estimate the representation geometry and calibrate editability, plus implementation complexity over existing editing libraries. It can fail if the assumed low-rank structure does not hold for a given model, if editability is miscalibrated (hard edits fail or easy edits corrupt pretrained knowledge), or if the method's benefits do not transfer beyond the evaluated GPT2-XL/GPT-J/LLaMA-3-8B settings.

The paper states GEdit 'consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both editing success and knowledge preservation' across GPT2-XL, GPT-J, and LLaMA-3-8B with up to 10,000 sequential edits, but the abstract provides no quantified improvement factor.
